findings.evidence: "The most recent version supersedes the one that came before it."
findings.fix: Either explain what creates a new version of the reimbursement log, or remove the sentence.
findings.violation: This sentence refers to a "version" of the reimbursement log without ever establishing that multiple versions exist or what triggers a new one, so the referent is unclear.

findings.evidence: "The stipend covers one claim per employee per benefit year" versus "the policy applies to one device per category per employee"
findings.fix: State a single, unambiguous limit, for example "one claim per employee per benefit year, covering at most one device per equipment category."
findings.location: Eligibility, first paragraph, compared with Restrictions and Exceptions
findings.violation: It is unclear whether an employee gets one claim total per year or one claim per equipment category per year; the two statements describe different limits and are never reconciled.

findings.evidence: "The stipend clock resumes on their first day back."
findings.fix: Name the specific timer explicitly, for example "the 90 day service waiting period resumes counting on their first day back."
findings.violation: "Stipend clock" is used without being defined anywhere earlier in the document, so a reader cannot tell which timer (the 90 day service requirement, the annual claim limit, or something else) is being described.

findings.evidence: "the stipend request, once the manager signs it, after finance confirms the budget line, moves to final processing"
findings.fix: Rewrite as a simple ordered sequence, for example "The manager signs the request, finance then confirms the budget line, and the request then moves to final processing."
findings.violation: The nested clause ordering makes it ambiguous whether the manager signs before or after finance confirms the budget line.

findings.evidence: "The employee receives a confirmation email once processing finishes" and "the employee reviews the confirmation summary before submitting the final request"
findings.fix: Describe a single sequence of events, making clear that the pre-submission review and the post-processing email are two separate, clearly labeled notifications.
findings.location: How to Apply, second and third paragraphs
findings.violation: These two statements contradict each other on when the employee sees a confirmation: one places it after processing finishes, the other places it before the final request is even submitted.

findings.evidence: "The requester gets an automatic reminder after three days."
findings.fix: State the reference point explicitly, for example "three days after the request is marked incomplete."
findings.violation: The document does not state what the three days are measured from, whether the original submission date or the date the request was marked incomplete.

findings.evidence: "A photo of the receipt is enough for most requests."
findings.fix: Name the specific category or dollar threshold that requires additional documentation, or remove the qualifier if a photo is always sufficient.
findings.violation: "Most requests" does not identify which requests need something beyond a photo, so an employee cannot determine their own documentation requirement in advance.

findings.evidence: "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Rewrite in third person to match the rest of the document, for example "Employees must keep equipment in good working condition, and the benefits team may request a brief photo check once a year."
findings.violation: This sentence switches to second person, "you" and "we," while every other section of the policy uses third person, "employees," "the finance office," creating an inconsistent voice.

findings.evidence: "Finance reconciles the reimbursable item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the covered purchase amount after that monthly review."
findings.fix: Pick one term for the purchased item and use it consistently throughout the policy.
findings.violation: The document uses three different terms, "stipend item," "reimbursable item," and "covered purchase," for what appears to be the same equipment purchase, without ever stating they are the same thing.

findings.evidence: "Also, you submit the request in the portal. Countersign the employee request within two business days."
findings.fix: Use third person consistently and reuse the verb already established for the manager's action instead of introducing "countersign."
findings.violation: This paragraph switches to second person again and introduces "countersign" as a new, subjectless action that is never connected to the "reviews" and "confirms" language already used for the manager's step in Approval Timeline.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and the uploaded receipt."
findings.fix: Rewrite as a complete parallel construction, for example "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility and uploading the receipt."
findings.violation: The sentence is grammatically incomplete because "the uploaded receipt" has no verb, so it is unclear whether the employee is expected to upload the receipt, review it, or something else.

findings.evidence: "The IT asset group updates the equipment catalog after every open enrollment period."
findings.fix: State a single owner and a single update cadence for the equipment catalog, and remove the conflicting statement.
findings.violation: This conflicts with Program Overview, which states the benefits team publishes the equipment catalog on the first business day of the month; the document never reconciles who owns the catalog or how often it actually changes.

findings.evidence: "Every entry carries a date stamp so the record stays easy to audit."
findings.fix: Delete the repeated sentence from this section.
findings.violation: This sentence duplicates, almost word for word, a sentence already given in Program Overview, adding no new information here.

findings.evidence: "A separate audit last spring reviewed unrelated travel expenses. Federal guidance on remote work continues to evolve each year. The office coffee budget was reset at the start of the quarter."
findings.fix: Remove these sentences, or explain explicitly how they connect to the stipend program if they belong here at all.
findings.violation: These sentences are unrelated to the home office equipment stipend policy and give a reader no actionable information about the program.

findings.evidence: "The finance office also flags any request that repeats within the same quarter."
findings.fix: Clarify what "repeats" refers to, for example a second request from the same employee or a duplicate submission of the same request, or remove the rule if it cannot occur under the one claim per year limit.
findings.violation: Eligibility states the stipend covers only one claim per employee per benefit year, so it is unclear how a request could repeat within the same quarter, leaving this rule describing a situation the rest of the document says cannot happen.

findings.evidence: "The finance liaison publishes the vendor list on the first business day of the month. The most recent version supersedes the one that came before it."
findings.fix: Either define what the vendor list is and how employees use it, or remove this section.
findings.violation: This introduces a "vendor list" that is never mentioned or defined anywhere else in the document, and reuses the same sentence structure already used for the equipment catalog and the reimbursement log, reading as templated filler rather than information specific to this policy.
